turns.text: Welcome to the interview.
Welcome, thanks. Ready when you are.
What time did you go to bed last night?
Went to bed around 10:30, like most nights. Fell asleep pretty fast too, I was beat.
Approximately how many hours did you sleep last night? Would you say you slept well? Why or why not?

Slept maybe five hours, five and a half if I'm generous. Woke up right on schedule around 3:30 like clockwork, mind going over the shop's numbers, and then it was in and out until the alarm. So — okay, not great, but that's just how it goes for me most nights.
What was the last activity you engaged in before going to bed? And why did you choose to do that activity?
Went with the phone thriller thing — reading for a bit in bed before lights out. It's just a habit at this point, helps my eyes get heavy without me having to think about it.
That sounds like a nice routine. What was the book or story you were reading on your phone?
"Just some cheap thriller novel, nothing fancy — honestly couldn't tell you the title if you asked me, one of those airport-paperback types you download and forget."

Thanks for explaining that. 

What factors have most affected your sleep quality over the past two weeks?

Honestly, the biggest thing's just the shop — end of month numbers, ordering stock, that kind of stuff running through my head at 3:30. House being emptier since the kids left probably doesn't help either, more quiet to notice it in. Otherwise nothing's really changed — same beer with dinner most nights, same routine.
Is this pretty typical for you, or has something changed recently with your sleep over the past few months?

Pretty typical for me — this has been the pattern for years, ever since the shop got going. Doesn't really shift much month to month, kids leaving just made the quiet part of it more noticeable, that's all.
Overall, are you happy with how you are sleeping these days? Why or why not?

Honestly, yeah, mostly — I sleep enough to get through the day, and I've been doing this long enough it doesn't rattle me. Would I take eight hours straight through if you offered it to me? Sure. But I don't lose sleep over losing sleep, if that makes sense.
You’ve probably heard the advice that adults should get 7–9 hours of sleep a night. Does that feel practical for you right now?

Yeah, honestly, no — not with the hours I keep. Between opening at 7 and closing at 6, six days a week, plus the 3:30 wake-up, I'm doing more like six, six and a half most nights. Nice idea on paper, but I'd have to close the shop early to hit that, and that's not happening.
Many people check their mobile phones, tablets, or computers right before bed. Do you do this, too? Why or why not?
Not really, no — phone stays out on the charger in the kitchen once I go up. Old habit, I guess, or maybe just too tired by 10:30 to bother scrolling anything.
Do you regularly use social media at other times of day? If so, how do you typically use it, especially in the hours before bed?

Not really — I've got Facebook, mostly to keep an eye on the shop's page and see if anyone's messaged about an order, but I'm not scrolling for fun. If I'm on it, it's during the day at the counter when it's slow, not in the evening. By the time we close up and eat dinner, honestly, I'm more interested in the TV or that book than my phone.

Thanks for explaining that.

Now a couple of quick questions about technology in general: Do you regularly use AI chatbots, like ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, or similar apps?
Not really — I've messed around with one a couple times, honestly, but it's not something I use day to day. Running the shop keeps me busy enough without adding another screen to stare at.

Thanks for sharing that.

If you could improve one thing about your sleeping habits, what would it be?
If I could fix one thing, it'd be that 3:30 wake-up — cutting out that hour or two of lying there dozing would make the biggest difference. The falling asleep part's never been the issue for me.
Given your work and daily responsibilities with the shop, do you think reducing or getting rid of that 3:30 wake-up would be doable? Why or why not?

Doable, sure — probably not gone completely, but I bet I could take the edge off it. Realistically the shop stuff isn't going anywhere while I'm running it, but I could maybe do something like not checking the till numbers right before bed, or actually writing down what's bugging me instead of chewing on it at 3:30. Haven't really tried, if I'm honest — it's just become part of the routine, like the alarm going off.

Thanks for explaining that.

Now a few quick background questions. (Feel free to skip anything you’d rather not share.)

What is your age?
Thank you. What is your profession?
I run a small hardware and DIY supply shop with my wife — nuts and bolts, paint, tools, that sort of thing. Been doing it for years now.
Thanks. What country were you born in?
Poland — born and raised here, near Kraków actually.
Thank you. What country do you currently live in?
Poland — same as always, near Kraków.

Thanks for sharing all of that. Those are all the interview questions I had.

Before we wrap up, is there anything else you’d like to add about your sleep or daily routine that we haven’t talked about?
